subject: Hosted availability uplift & fixed-credit schedule — terms discussion
messages:
From: Elaine Torres <elaine.torres@datapulse.io>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia+redwood@dataplane.redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Datapulse Legal <contracts@datapulse.io>
Date: Fri, 01 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: hosted SLA uplift to 99.99% + fixed credit cap

Sofia / Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo — the latency numbers look promising. Before we proceed to procurement we need to reconcile a few items in your standard hosted SLA template:

• Uptime: Datapulse requires 99.99% monthly uptime for the inference endpoints used by our fraud scoring service (hosted tenancy).
• Fixed credits: instead of a percentage TBD, we want a dollar-denominated credit schedule capped at 8% of our monthly invoice for platform-attributable incidents.
• Latency SLO: p99 <150ms for text-generation endpoints (30-day rolling window).
• Maintenance: 72-hour notice for planned maintenance affecting our tenant; total planned maintenance cannot exceed 2 hours per month.

I attached a short matrix from our SRE showing how each item maps to risk and procurement thresholds (Datapulse_request_matrix.xlsx). If Redwood cannot accept hosted 99.99%, we need a measurable remediation path (credits + migration timeline to Dedicated with pinned capacity).

Can we schedule 30 mins early next week to align on feasible options?

Best,
Elaine
Head of Platform Reliability, Datapulse
elaine.torres@datapulse.io
Attachments: Datapulse_request_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12KB)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia+redwood@dataplane.redwood.com>
To: Elaine Torres <elaine.torres@datapulse.io>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 01 May 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: hosted SLA uplift to 99.99% + fixed credit cap

Hi Elaine,

Appreciate the clear ask and the matrix 33 that helps. Quick summary from our side:

• Hosted vs Dedicated: Our published hosted SLA is 99.95%. Reaching 99.99% in hosted mode for production-scale inference is exceptionally rare without dedicated reserved capacity and specific network topology guarantees.
• Credit structure: We typically operate a graduated credit table (percentage of monthly invoice based on monthly availability bands) with a cap to limit correlated exposure. We can consider an alternative contract exhibit that translates that into a fixed-dollar schedule tied to invoice amount and cap it at 8% for the initial 12-month term.
• Latency: Committing to p99 <150ms on hosted endpoints depends on model size, batch characteristics, and tenant co-tenancy. We can offer a latency credit for measured p99 degradations, but guaranteeing 150ms on hosted requires Dedicated pools.
• Maintenance windows: 72h notice for planned maintenance is reasonable for Dedicated; hosted has a published maintenance policy with advance notice and emergency exclusions.

Attached: Redwood_SLA_Template_v2.pdf with inline comments. I
 can propose a DocuSign-ready exhibit that either: (A) offers hosted with a conservative credit schedule tied to your 8% cap and an agreed remediation plan; or (B) moves you to a Dedicated reserved-capacity exhibit that supports higher availability/latency commitments.

Would Monday 10:00am PT work for a 30-min sync?

Thanks,
Sofia
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sofia+redwood@dataplane.redwood.com
Attachments: Redwood_SLA_Template_v2.pdf (PDF, 55KB)

From: Elaine Torres <elaine.torres@datapulse.io>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia+redwood@dataplane.redwood.com>
Cc: Datapulse Legal <contracts@datapulse.io>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 02 May 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: hosted SLA uplift to 99.99% + fixed credit cap

Sofia,

Thanks 3 for the quick reply. A couple of clarifications after an internal alignment with Procurement and Legal:

• Data residency: Datapulse requires staying in the hosted tenancy for the next 12 months for data-residency reasons. Moving to Dedicated is not an option during that period.
• Fixed cap: the 8% cap must be explicit in the SLA and expressed as a dollar cap (8% of monthly invoice) rather than a non-binding note.
• Latency: p99 <150ms is a hard functional requirement for our fraud model. If Redwood cannot commit to that in hosted mode we need an SLA credit tied to degraded p99 latency tiers.

I've attached an updated request matrix with proposed credit numbers and escalation contacts (Datapulse_request_matrix.xlsx). If you cannot accept hosted-mode 99.99%, please propose a measurable remediation path (e.g., fixed credits + guaranteed migration path to Dedicated within X months with priority onboarding).

Best,
Elaine
Attachments: Datapulse_request_matrix.xlsx (updated)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia+redwood@dataplane.redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 02 May 2026 11:14:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Hosted availability uplift & fixed-credit schedule — input needed

Team, forwarding Elaine's asks from Datapulse. Key negotiation points: hosted 99.99% ask (data residency blocks Dedicated), dollar-denominated credit capped at 8%, mandatory p99 <150ms target or latency-credit alternative, and tighter maintenance rules.

Marcus 5 could you run a quick feasibility check on whether we can architect tenant-level isolation in hosted to materially reduce co-tenancy noise? Laura / Rishi please advise on how far Legal can go on explicit dollar caps vs percentage exhibits. Planning to propose two tracks for Monday: a commercial exhibit (fixed-dollar schedule capped at 8% for 12 months) + technical remediation plan (latency monitoring and escalation path).

Thanks,
Sofia

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia+redwood@dataplane.redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 03 May 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosted availability uplift & fixed-credit schedule — input needed

Sofia / all,

Quick technical note: achieving deterministic p99 <150ms on hosted is non-trivial at scale, but there are mitigations we can responsibly offer that materially reduce risk:

1) Tenant affinity pins: allow Datapulse inference traffic to be routed preferentially to a narrow set of hosts with warm KV caches for their model family. This is a best-effort mechanism in hosted but reduces noisy neighbor variance.
2) Dedicated network lanes: introduce optional egress/network QoS for their region to reduce network jitter (adds cost).
3) Measurement & credit tie: instrument p99 at the per-tenant edge, 30-day rolling window, and establish latency bands with fixed-dollar credits per band. Example proposal:
   - p99 <=150ms: no credit
   - 150ms < p99 <=250ms: $X per incident / month (to be defined against monthly invoice)
   - p99 >250ms: larger credit + escalation to reliability SWAT

From an ops perspective we can commit to 72-hour notice for planned maintenance and limit planned host-level maintenance impacting the tenant to 2 hours per calendar month if they commit to a certain spend/term and sign the exhibit.

I'll draft a short commercial exhibit and a technical appendix for Monday. Marcus

Attachments: SLA_redline.docx (DOCX, 18KB)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Torres <elaine.torres@datapulse.io>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia+redwood@dataplane.redwood.com>, Datapulse Legal <contracts@datapulse.io>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 03 May 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted availability uplift & fixed-credit schedule — proposal

Elaine / Datapulse team,

Thanks for the candid requirements and the matrix. Based on our internal review we can offer the following narrow package for a 12-month term while you remain in hosted tenancy: 

1) Availability: a hosted availability target of 99.99% for the specified inference endpoints, with a definition of "platform-attributable outage" scoped tightly in the exhibit.
2) Credit schedule: fixed-dollar credit table tied to monthly invoice with an absolute cap of 8% of monthly invoice for recurring monthly credits. Credits will be paid as service credits on the next invoice.
3) Latency SLO: instrumented p99 measured at the edge, with a two-band credit schedule (150-250ms, >250ms). Credits for latency violations will be defined as fixed dollar amounts in the exhibit.
4) Maintenance: 72-hour notice for planned maintenance that could affect the tenant; planned maintenance impacting tenant capacity limited to 2 hours/month. Emergency maintenance and force majeure remain exclusions.

We will provide a redlined SLA exhibit and an operations appendix that includes the tenant-affinity and network-lane options Marcus suggested. To proceed quickly, we propose: (A) Redwood sends a DocuSign-ready SLA exhibit with the fixed-credit table and measurement language by Monday afternoon; (B) Datapulse reviews and provides any final redlines within 48 hours; (C) mutual execution and a prioritized onboarding slot for tenant-affinity routing.

If that approach works, I'll loop in Finance to confirm billing mechanics and Laura to finalize contract language.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
Attachments: (none)

Subject: Re: Hosted availability uplift & fixed-credit schedule — proposal

Rishi / Sofia,

This is helpful and addresses the majority of our concerns. A few quick asks before we sign: please ensure the credit table maps to sample dollar figures (we will validate against our expected monthly invoice) and that the latency-measurement methodology is unambiguous (edge measurement points, sampling, and aggregation window). Also confirm that credits are paid as an invoice credit (not future one-off refunds) and that the 8% cap is absolute for recurring monthly credits.

If you can send the DocuSign exhibit and the operations appendix with explicit measurement definitions by Monday, we will aim to return a final redline within 48 hours.

Thanks,
Elaine
Head of Platform Reliability, Datapulse
Attachments: none
